newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FOCUS-Ireland's TV3 confident despite setback.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ireland's TV3 confident despite setback.

text.p: A consortium planning a third television channel in Ireland said on Wednesday it was confident of going on air next year despite the abrupt withdrawal of Northern Ireland's Ulster Television Plc.
"It is still quite realistic that we will be on air by next year," RTV consortium spokesman and shareholder James Morris said.
"Now that Ulster TV has pulled out it leaves us with a need and we will be looking for a replacement broadcast partner."
He was speaking after Northern Ireland's independent news and entertaintment channel, UTV, announced in its annual results statement that it was pulling out of the TV3 consortium.
The consortium said the main area of dispute had been UTV's level of control and the extent to which the association of UTV with TV3 might lead to distortions in the market place.

"Unfortunately this particular deal has fallen through, but it is on other issues rather than viability and a number of people contacted us over the last year and we said to them we have an agreement with UTV so we didn't enter into any discussions with them," Morris said.
"We will be renewing those contacts and we have already had some contacts today."

UTV announced its participation in the consortium last September and was understood to have committed itself to taking a 40 percent stake worth approximately 6.0 million pounds ($9.35 million), making it the largest single shareholder.
UTV was seen as a key player in the operation because it would have brought programme-making and technical expertise to the fledgling channel.

In its statement UTV said the group had submitted a business plan to Ireland's Independent Radio and Television Commission (IRTC) but some of the terms of the UTV/TV3 agreement were unacceptable to the IRTC.
"Our board feels the risks associated with proceeding with the proposal on the terms required by the IRTC would not be in the interests of either the company or the shareholders," UTV said.

A one third shareholding is now expected to be made available to institutional investors, with the rest of the equity held by the manager of Irish rock band U2, Paul McGuinness, James Morris of Windmill Lane Studios and accountant Ossie Kilkenny.
The group has been awarded the exclusive right to negotiate over the granting of a television programme service contract for a new national independent television channel in Ireland.
Morris said the main revenue would be generated by advertising and estimated the current total television advertising market at around 80-90 million punts.
Semi-state owned RTE currently holds the monopoly on the Republic's two existing channels RTE 1 and Network 2. ($1=.6415 Pound)
